title: Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peers
web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comparisons
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: What does the November 20 close of $77.80 imply about Bitcoin, fixed preferred charges, and a broken equity premium?

epigraph.quote: The tipping point for share-accretive issuances and purchases is an mNAV of just above 1.0.
epigraph.author: Henry T. C. Hu, Strategy's Bitcoin Treasury Model (2026) [38]

web_blocks.html: Start with the clean November 20, 2026 market cutoff. MSTR closed at $77.80, down 9.67% on the day and 30.30% for the week. Bitcoin closed the same session at $58,798.98, down 16.98% from $70,822.24 on November 12. That move pushed Strategy's 850,849 Bitcoin holdings 22.1% below its $75,452 average purchase cost. At $77.80, the common equity no longer commands a premium over net treasury value. [14][40][42][50][54]

Split-adjusted prices show how sharply MSTR swings when Bitcoin and capital-market access turn together. From $12.36 on August 10, 2020, the stock surged 742% to $104.10 in February 2021. It then fell 86.4% to $14.16 by December 30, 2022. From there it rallied 3,247% to $473.83 on November 20, 2024, before dropping 67.9% to $151.95 at year-end 2025. By November 20, 2026, it had fallen another 48.8% year to date to $77.80. [40][41][42]

web_blocks.title: Live November 20 asset-coverage and mNAV bridge

web_blocks.html: A software DCF cannot anchor MSTR because Software operating cash flow is negative before treasury interest. Instead, we mark Strategy's latest disclosed holdings and senior claims to the November 20 session. As of November 15, Strategy held 850,849 Bitcoin ($64.20 billion cost), a $4.75 billion USD Reserve, and $151.2 million USD Cash. Against that stand $6.75 billion of convertible debt principal and $13.484 billion of adjusted preferred liquidation preference. [2][50][54]

web_blocks.caption: Table 7.2: November 20, 2026 Live Asset-Coverage and mNAV Bridge (USD billions unless noted)
rows: Down $10.20B from Nov. 12 gross BTC value.
Unpledged reserve covers ~38 months of fixed charges.
6.262M STRC shares retired at $100 par; unadjusted is $14.110B.
Excludes software value and $1.51B-$1.59B annual fixed burn.
Drops to $77.51 after 1 year of $1.55B fixed charges.
4.1% discount to static NAV; 1.004x post 1-yr burn.
Below 1.00x tipping point; ATM equity issuance is dilutive.
web_blocks.takeaway: At $77.80 and $58,798.98 Bitcoin, MSTR trades at 0.972x EV/BTC mNAV, breaking the >1.0x equity-issuance engine and turning ATM sales dilutive per share. [2][38][50][54]

web_blocks.html: Why did the stock fall below static residual value? First, static residual NAV ignores $1.51 billion to $1.59 billion in annual preferred dividends and convertible interest. Subtracting one year of that $1.55 billion midpoint drag reduces residual equity to $77.51 per share, right at the $77.80 close. Second, issuing Class A stock below 1.0x mNAV to pay 12% STRC dividends or buy back STRC at par erodes common-share Bitcoin backing. Third, expected November 2026 MSCI index exclusion threatens forced passive outflows just as spot ETFs offer 0.25% fee access. [2][39][50]

web_blocks.the_number: 12-month Base Fair Value: $76.34 per share (-1.9% vs. $77.80 CMP); Probability-Weighted Value: $66.86 per share (-14.1% vs. CMP).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We project 12-month Bitcoin value under Bear (-40%), Base (+10%), and Bull (+50%) scenarios, multiply by post-MSCI exit EV/BTC ratios (0.70x, 0.90x, 1.15x), deduct $1.55 billion of annual preferred dividends and interest from USD Assets, subtract $6.750 billion debt and $13.484 billion preferred preference, and divide by 427.672 million basic-equivalent shares.
web_blocks.the_inputs: 850,849 BTC at $58,798.98 ($50.029B), $4.901B USD Assets, $6.750B debt, $13.484B adjusted preferred preference, $1.550B annual fixed-charge drag, 427.672M shares, and scenario weights of 40% Bear, 40% Base, and 20% Bull.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear $9.66 per share (-87.6% if BTC drops 40% and mNAV compresses to 0.70x); Base $76.34 (-1.9% at +10% BTC and 0.90x mNAV); Bull $162.32 (+108.6% if BTC rallies 50% and mNAV recovers to 1.15x).
web_blocks.if_off: If Bitcoin clears Strategy's $75,452 average cost and mNAV returns above 1.15x without equity dilution, fair value rises toward the Bull range; if MSCI exclusion triggers steeper discounts or 2027 put refinancing stress, equity value compresses toward the Bear tail. Note also that our $76.34 Base case freezes shares at 427.672M and omits standalone software cash burn (-$67.241M in FY2025); modeling 10% Class A dilution (470.439M shares) plus -$67.241M software burn lowers 12-month Base equity value to $69.25 per share (-11.0% vs CMP).

web_blocks.takeaway: Even assuming +10% Bitcoin appreciation, a realistic 0.90x post-MSCI exit multiple and $1.55B annual fixed-charge burn leave Base value at $76.34—and adding 10% share dilution plus -$67.241M software CFO burn lowers Base fair value to $69.25 (-11.0% vs. CMP). [2][50][54]

web_blocks.title: Peer snapshot: software compounders vs. crypto proxies

web_blocks.html: Comparing MSTR against enterprise software vendors (Microsoft, Salesforce, Teradata) and Coinbase underscores why valuation cannot rest on software multiples. At $77.80, MSTR trades at 66.37x trailing software sales and 0.59x price-to-book, with negative operating margins (-8.7%) and negative ROE (-21.6%). Meanwhile, Coinbase has also dropped into Stage 4 (-47.6% revenue YoY, -32.6% OPM), whereas Microsoft and Teradata show positive operating margins. [41][42]

web_blocks.caption: Table 7.4: MSTR vs. Software & Crypto Operating Peers (Nov. 20, 2026 Snapshot)
web_blocks.takeaway: MSFT (25.3x P/E, 47.1% OPM) and TDC (7.5x P/E, Stage 2) price recurring software cash flow, while MSTR and COIN both sit in Stage 4 with negative margins. [41][42]

web_blocks.region_era: United States, 2021–2024 closed-end Bitcoin trust cycle
web_blocks.mechanism: A non-redeemable Bitcoin vehicle traded above asset value during inflows, then flipped to a severe discount once rival wrappers offered lower friction and no forced lockup.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: GBTC swung from premiums above 40% in 2020 to a record discount exceeding 50% in December 2022 before its January 2024 ETF conversion narrowed the gap to 0.10%. [36][37]
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Unlike GBTC, MSTR cannot convert into a redeemable spot ETF because it carries $6.75B of debt and $13.48B of preferred stock; sub-1.0x discounts can persist.

web_blocks.title: VALUATION TAKEAWAY
paragraphs: At 0.972x EV/BTC mNAV, Strategy has lost its equity-issuance premium. Until Bitcoin clears cost or fixed charges shrink without dilutive common sales, the math favors staying away. [2][38][50]

book_paragraphs: Valuation starts with the November 20, 2026 close of $77.80. In just six trading sessions after November 12, MSTR fell 32.0%, slicing through its prior $88 to $94 watch band and its $79.00 structural stop. Over the same eight calendar days, Bitcoin dropped 16.98% from $70,822.24 to $58,798.98. That decline pushed Strategy's 850,849 Bitcoin holdings 22.1% below its $75,452 average purchase price, creating an unrealized mark-to-market deficit of roughly $14.17 billion against purchase cost. [40][42][50][54]

History reminds us that this magnitude of drawdown is not an anomaly for MSTR. On a split-adjusted basis, the stock surged from $12.36 in August 2020 to $104.10 in February 2021, then collapsed 86.4% to $14.16 by December 2022. It then climbed 3,247% to $473.83 in November 2024 before dropping 67.9% in 2025 and another 48.8% year to date through November 20, 2026. These violent swings reflect leveraged exposure to both Bitcoin price cycles and changes in the market's willingness to pay above net asset value. [40][42]

Because the enterprise software segment generated negative operating cash flow before treasury interest, a conventional software discounted-cash-flow model would misstate what drives the equity. Instead, we build a transparent November 20 balance-sheet bridge. Gross Bitcoin value equals 850,849 coins multiplied by $58,798.98, or $50.029 billion. Adding $4.750 billion in USD Reserve and $151.2 million in USD Cash as of November 15 yields $54.930 billion in gross treasury assets. [2][50][54]

Senior claims take the first $20.234 billion off the top. Convertible debt principal sits at $6.750 billion per Note 6 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. Preferred stock carries a $14.110 billion liquidation preference at September 30 per Note 10, which adjusts down to $13.484 billion after subtracting 6,262,009 STRC shares repurchased at $100 par between October 26 and November 15. Dividing the $34.697 billion static residual across 427.672 million basic-equivalent shares yields $81.13 per share. [2][50]

At $77.80, the stock trades at 0.959x static residual NAV and 0.972x company-style EV-to-Bitcoin mNAV. That cross below 1.00x is a structural inflection. As Henry Hu's 2026 legal analysis notes, issuing common stock only builds per-share Bitcoin backing when mNAV sits above 1.00x. Below parity, selling shares to fund 12% STRC dividends or STRC buybacks dilutes common holders—consistent with Strategy's negative 4.2% year-to-date BTC Yield. [12][38][50]

A static bridge also omits ongoing cash burn. Management estimates $1.51 billion to $1.59 billion in annual preferred dividends and convertible interest. Deducting a $1.55 billion one-year midpoint reduces residual common value to $77.51 per share—nearly identical to the $77.80 close. Meanwhile, Strategy expects MSCI to remove its Class A stock from the Global Investable Market Indexes in November 2026, adding forced passive supply while spot ETFs like IBIT charge just 0.25%. [2][39]

Our 12-month scenario model reflects these real frictions rather than assuming a free premium. In the Base case (+10% Bitcoin to $64,679, 0.90x post-MSCI EV/BTC multiple, minus $1.55 billion fixed charges), implied equity value is $76.34 per share—1.9% below today's close. In the Bear case (-40% Bitcoin, 0.70x EV/BTC), senior claims amplify the loss down to $9.66 per share. In the Bull case (+50% Bitcoin, 1.15x EV/BTC), value rebounds to $162.32. Weighting these 40% Bear, 40% Base, and 20% Bull yields an expected value of $66.86 per share, or 14.1% downside. [2][50][54] Notice that this $76.34 Base estimate holds shares static at 427.672 million and excludes standalone software cash burn; modeling 10% Class A dilution (to 470.439 million shares) alongside FY2025's -$67.241 million operating cash burn reduces 12-month Base fair value to $69.25 per share (-11.0% vs. CMP).

The peer table highlights why MSTR cannot fall back on software multiples for support. Microsoft trades at 25.3x earnings with a 47.1% operating margin, and Teradata trades at 7.5x earnings in a Stage 2 uptrend. Strategy trades at 66.4x trailing software sales with a negative 8.7% operating margin and negative 21.6% return on equity. Coinbase shares MSTR's Stage 4 downtrend and negative margins, confirming severe sector-wide crypto pressure. [41][42]

Grayscale Bitcoin Trust offers the cleanest historical failure-mode parallel. When GBTC lacked daily redemptions and faced lower-fee competition, its premium flipped to a discount exceeding 50% in December 2022. Strategy faces an even harder constraint: because it owes $20.23 billion in senior debt and preferred claims, it cannot simply convert into a redeemable ETF to close a discount. [36][37]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a leveraged treasury vehicle breaks below 1.0x mNAV, cheapness is an illusion. Selling common stock below asset value shrinks rather than compounds Bitcoin per share. [38][50]
